title: Optimization Suggestions beta rollout plan + GA criteria (Console)
creator: Aditya Rao
description:
Context
We are shipping a private beta of the Console “Optimization suggestions” experience (batching + caching only) to make cost optimization actionable while preserving latency/reliability trust. This ticket defines (1) staged rollout cohorts, (2) feature flag strategy + guardrails/rollback, and (3) GA criteria.

Scope reminders (beta)
- Suggestions only for batching + caching (no quantization UI in this view).
- No automatic application; user must confirm changes via config pages / rollout controls.
- No contractual/guaranteed savings claims.

Rollout principles
- Safety first: start with dogfood + low-risk accounts, and progressively expand while watching API health, estimator sanity, and support load.
- Trust first: conservative defaults; clear “estimated” language; risk level explicitly refers to performance/reliability (not security).
- Measured learning loop: event instrumentation is a release gate (impression/expand/dismiss/apply-click + suggested_config_view).

Feature flag strategy
1) Primary gating (per-org)
- Flag name: console.optimize_suggestions_beta
- Type: per-org allowlist (no percentage rollout initially)
- Default: OFF
- Owner for enable/disable: Product (Marissa) + SRE (Sean) for emergency rollback
- Audit requirements:
  - Flag change must be logged with org_id, actor, timestamp, reason
  - For external enables, include ticket/reference (e.g., customer request / beta outreach)

2) Secondary gating (capability/data readiness)
- Suggestions may still be hidden/empty based on eligibility checks:
  - Required telemetry present (request volume threshold + latency distribution + cache metrics)
  - Compute job freshness (stale_as_of within threshold)
  - RBAC: optimize:suggestions:read permission
- UX must show deterministic empty states with “why” + setup CTA (no silent failure).

3) Kill switch / degradation
- Global kill switch: optimize_suggestions_global_off (backend + UI)
- If estimator pipeline is degraded, show last-good data and mark “stale” with staleness banner; if beyond max staleness, show “temporarily unavailable” empty state.

Staged rollout plan (proposed)
Stage 0 — Internal dogfood (Week 5)
- Cohort: Redwood internal orgs + 2–3 partner engineers who can validate copy/flows
- Entry criteria:
  - API + UI behind flags deployed to prod
  - Dashboard basics live (API p95, 5xx, compute lag, funnel)
- Exit criteria:
  - No Sev-2+ incidents attributable to suggestions
  - API p95 within budget for 72 hours
  - At least 10 internal sessions with structured feedback

Stage 1 — Friendly beta (Week 6)
- Cohort size: ~5 orgs
- Selection criteria:
  - High spend / cost sensitivity
  - Telemetry maturity (meets eligibility checks)
  - Willingness to provide feedback + join 30-min weekly check-in
  - Mix of use cases: latency-sensitive vs throughput-oriented
- Enablement steps:
  - PM/CS confirms eligibility + comms
  - SRE/PM enables per-org flag
  - CS provides “How estimates work” explainer + known limitations
- Monitoring focus:
  - Estimator plausibility (sanity checks vs historical billing deltas)
  - Confusion around risk label / expectations

Stage 2 — Expanded private beta (Week 7–8)
- Cohort size: 15–25 orgs
- Add a small number of larger/enterprise-like orgs (Arkadia-type) but still opt-in
- Introduce a constrained “percentage within allowlisted org” if needed to manage load (optional)
- Add stricter escalation path + support macros for “estimate seems off”

Stage 3 — Public beta (post-criteria)
- Feature discoverable in Console but still flagged by default for existing orgs; new orgs optionally see onboarding gate
- Potentially switch allowlist to staged percentage rollout if and only if system health + support load stable

Stage 4 — GA
- Feature on by default for eligible orgs
- SLA / contractual language remains out of scope; GA means product readiness (stability + clarity + acceptable estimation error bands)

Rollout ops + comms
- Customer-facing language must say “estimated savings” and include caveats + confidence bands when available.
- All enables must be tracked in a shared beta roster (org_id, owner, enable date, eligibility notes, feedback status).
- Weekly beta triage: Product (Marissa, Aditya), Eng (Dylan, Chloe), Applied ML (Maya/Jonas), Telemetry (Logan/Nadia), CS (Miguel), Support (Dev).

GA criteria (must meet all)
A) Reliability / performance (2 consecutive weeks)
- Suggestions API:
  - p95 latency <= agreed budget (see performance budget doc) in steady state
  - 5xx rate <= 0.5% daily and no sustained spikes > 2% for > 10 minutes without mitigation
- Compute pipeline:
  - Compute lag within target (no more than 2 missed cadences/week)
  - stale_as_of exceeds threshold for < 2% of suggestion views
- Console:
  - No Sev-2+ incidents caused by Suggestions UI (render loops, crashes, authz leakage)

B) Security / access control
- RBAC validated: users without optimize:suggestions:read cannot view list/details (including deep links).
- Org/project scoping validated: no cross-tenant leakage in API or UI.
- Audit logging in place for flag changes (and sampled access logs for endpoint).

C) Estimation quality + trust
- Estimator validation meets acceptance thresholds from validation plan:
  - Directionality: >= 90% of recommendations should be “non-negative savings” when applied under modeled assumptions
  - Calibration: median absolute percentage error (MAPE) under threshold agreed with Applied ML for top-quartile traffic routes
  - Guardrails: no aggressive batching suggestions for low-latency routes per constraints doc
- Support signal:
  - < 3% of enabled orgs file “estimate seems wrong” tickets in a 14-day period
  - All such tickets have a documented root cause category (data lag, pricing config mismatch, misunderstanding, bug)

D) Product usability (beta engagement + comprehension)
- Funnel health (per dashboard spec) for enabled orgs:
  - >= 30% of impressions lead to an expand within 7 days (signal: relevance)
  - Dismiss reasons collected for >= 60% of dismissals (signal: learnability)
  - >= 5% of expanded suggestions lead to apply-click / config deep link within 14 days (signal: actionability)
- UX research outcomes:
  - Users can correctly explain what “risk” means in this UI (performance/reliability) and how to mitigate
  - Users can find “assumptions/caveats” and understand estimates are not guarantees

E) Support readiness
- Support macros + internal runbook links published
- Known issues list maintained + referenced in release notes
- On-call escalation path defined for:
  - API latency regressions
  - compute lag/backfill issues
  - “empty but traffic is high” telemetry mismatch

Out of scope for GA (explicit)
- Quantization recommendations UI
- Auto-application of changes
- Savings commitments tied to contracts

Open questions
1) Eligibility thresholds: What is the minimum QPS/requests-per-day needed to avoid noisy estimates? (Owner: Nadia + Maya)
2) Confidence band display: Do we require confidence bands for GA, or can we GA with “confidence: low/med/high” only? (Owner: Aditya + Tessa)
3) Cohort mix: How many latency-sensitive customers can we safely include in Stage 2 without skewing feedback? (Owner: Marissa + Miguel)

Decision needed
- PM + Eng + SRE sign-off on GA gates (particularly estimator calibration thresholds) by 2026-02-28 so we can align release notes and support enablement.

Proposed next steps
- Marissa: finalize cohort roster + Stage 1 enable dates with CS (Miguel)
- Aditya/Maya: confirm estimator acceptance thresholds + define standard “sanity checks” run weekly
- Sean/Aisha: confirm alert thresholds and rollback criteria for p95 regression
- Dev/Elliot: finalize support macros + docs disclaimers alignment
acceptance_criteria: Rollout stages (0–4) and cohort selection criteria documented and aligned with Console + Optimize leads
Feature flag plan includes per-org allowlist, eligibility gating, kill switch, and auditing expectations
GA criteria defined across reliability, security/RBAC, estimation quality, usability, and support readiness with measurable thresholds
Rollout ownership + weekly beta triage cadence defined (PM/Eng/Applied ML/Telemetry/CS/Support)
Open questions have named owners and deadlines for resolution before Stage 1 enablement
rollout_stages: Stage 0: Internal dogfood (Redwood orgs) — validate UI, API health, copy comprehension
Stage 1: Friendly private beta (~5 orgs) — high-telemetry, cost-sensitive, feedback-friendly
Stage 2: Expanded private beta (15–25 orgs) — broaden mix, tighten support readiness
Stage 3: Public beta — discoverable, still staged/controlled
Stage 4: GA — on by default for eligible orgs
comments: 2026-02-06 (Marissa Cole): Drafted staged rollout proposal. Waiting on Telemetry to confirm compute lag SLO + eligibility thresholds. Added requirement that stale_as_of banner is mandatory for UI trust.

2026-02-11 (Sean Gallagher): Please add explicit rollback criteria for API p95 regression (e.g., >30% over baseline for 30m) and clarify kill switch ownership. We should treat this like any other Console surface with a rapid disable path.

2026-02-13 (Dr. Maya Srinivasan): GA gating should include calibration thresholds. We can commit to directionality + bounded error for top quartile routes, but not long-tail low-volume routes. Suggest defining a minimum traffic eligibility for GA.

2026-02-18 (Dev Patel): Support needs a clear macro for ‘estimate doesn’t match billing’ and an internal checklist (pricing config, staleness, token accounting differences). Please add “support readiness” as a GA gate, not a nice-to-have.
2026-02-21 (Aditya Rao): Updated GA criteria section to include estimator validation metrics and guardrails alignment. Still need final numbers for MAPE/thresholds and eligibility windows from Nadia.

2026-02-24 (Dylan Brooks): From Eng: OK with per-org allowlist + kill switch. Request: if compute pipeline is degraded, UI should not spam retries; show cached last-good result + banner and suppress detail fetch errors.
